official.deadline_note: Applications for the 2027 intake are closed. The programme runs one call a year; the most recent official factsheet advertised an application window of 1 February to 30 April, but no next-intake dates are published yet.
official.application_cycle: Annual round; the 2027 intake is closed and the next round has not yet opened
official.status_note: The ACIAR page states 'Applications closed' and 'Applications for the 2027 intake are now closed'; applications are submitted through the Online Australia Scholarships Information System (OASIS).
official.tuition_coverage_note: Fellowship benefits generally apply: full tuition fees, return air travel, an establishment allowance, a Contribution to Living Expenses, and the compulsory Introductory Academic Program.
benefits: Return air travel - payment of a single return, economy class airfare to and from Australia, via the most direct route
Establishment allowance - a once only payment as a contribution towards accommodation expenses, textbooks and study materials
Contribution to Living Expenses (CLE) - a fortnightly contribution to basic living expenses paid at a rate determined by the department
Introductory Academic Program (IAP) - a compulsory program prior to the commencement of formal academic studies covering information on living and studying in Australia
Additional pastoral care and development opportunities from ACIAR, and entry to the John Allwright Fellowship Executive Leadership Program
eligibility: Be a scientist or economist from an ACIAR partner country

Be currently or recently involved in an ACIAR research project (actively involved in an ACIAR research project or small research activity within the last 24 months; ACIAR may consider researchers from 'advanced pipeline' projects)
Seek admission to Masters by Research or PhD study at an Australian tertiary institution (Masters by coursework is not eligible)
Not be a citizen of Australia, hold Australian permanent residency, or be applying for a visa to live in Australia permanently
Be a citizen of the country in which you are working
Be currently employed on a permanent or long-term contract basis
Hold qualifications equivalent to at least an Australian Bachelor degree in a discipline relevant to the proposed area of postgraduate study
Be endorsed by your current employer, ACIAR project leaders (commissioned organisations and country collaborators) and your primary supervisor to apply
Have recently undertaken an English language test (IELTS, TOEFL or PTE), or be prepared to take the test on receipt of the application outcome
requirements: Register an account in the Online Australia Scholarships Information System (OASIS), log on, create and complete an application form
Select the ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships award program when starting the application

Research proposal must address how gender equity, social inclusion and climate change will be considered in the research approach and how the research contributes to a development priority of your country
Sign a contract with the Commonwealth of Australia agreeing to comply with the conditions of the scholarship
Applicants must read the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook, which covers general eligibility, selection processes, entitlements and responsibilities
Not providing the mandatory documents may impact eligibility
documents: OASIS application form with the ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships award program selected
Endorsements from your current employer, ACIAR project leaders and your primary supervisor
Research proposal addressing gender equity, social inclusion, climate change and your country's development priority
Evidence of qualifications equivalent to at least an Australian Bachelor degree in a relevant discipline
English language test result (IELTS, TOEFL or PTE) from the last 6 months, or a commitment to test on receipt of the outcome
selection_criteria: Competitive, merit-based program available to scientists or economists currently or recently involved in ACIAR research projects in partner countries
Selected by the Training Committee; applicants must be connected with an ACIAR project through current or recent work
In line with ACIAR's gender equity commitment, women now comprise at least half of new JAF award holders
The program is allocating places specifically for research dedicated to addressing climate change, climate adaptation or strengthening resilience to climate change impacts
coverage: Full tuition fees for the Masters by Research or PhD at the Australian tertiary institution
Contribution to basic living expenses (fortnightly, at a rate determined by the department)
Single return economy airfare to and from Australia via the most direct route
Once-only establishment allowance towards accommodation, textbooks and study materials
Compulsory Introductory Academic Program before formal studies begin
application_method: Read the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook before applying
Register an account in OASIS and log on to create and complete an application form
Select the ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships award program and submit before the round closes
Follow the OASIS Applicant User Guide for registration and application instructions
official.application_route: Online application through OASIS (Online Australia Scholarships Information System), selecting the ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships award program; enquiries to capacity.building@aciar.gov.au or your regional ACIAR office
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of the ACIAR partner country in which you work, and must not hold Australian citizenship or permanent residency
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Scientists or economists currently or recently involved in ACIAR research projects in partner countries; the research must address a development priority of your country
official.research_requirement: The research proposal must demonstrate how the research contributes to addressing a development priority of your country and must address gender equity, social inclusion and climate change in its approach and intended outcomes
official.duration: Offered for the minimum period necessary for the individual to complete the academic program specified by the Australian higher education institution, including any preparatory training
official.description: The John Allwright Fellowship is a competitive, merit-based program available to scientists or economists from partner countries currently or recently involved in ACIAR research projects, offering the opportunity to obtain formal postgraduate qualifications at an Australian tertiary institution. It provides Masters by Research or PhD scholarships administered through the Australia Awards system, with ACIAR providing additional pastoral care and development opportunities, and is the largest investment in the ACIAR Capacity Development Program.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research, administered through the Australia Awards system)
official.english_requirement: A recently undertaken English language test (IELTS, TOEFL or PTE), within the last 6 months at the time of applying, or preparedness to take the test on receipt of the application outcome

applicant_utility.summary: Eligibility runs through your ACIAR project connection: you must be a scientist or economist actively involved in an ACIAR research project or small research activity within the last 24 months, permanently employed, and endorsed by your employer, the ACIAR project leaders and your primary supervisor before you even open the OASIS form. Applications for the 2027 intake have closed, so the practical task is securing those endorsements and the English test now, since the round has historically opened 1 February and closed 30 April. Treat the research proposal's gender equity, social inclusion and climate-change framing as scored content, not boilerplate, and note that places are being allocated specifically for climate change, climate adaptation and resilience research.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Permanently employed scientists and economists in ACIAR partner countries who are working on current or recent ACIAR projects and want a research Master's or PhD at an Australian university.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your ACIAR project involvement falls within the last 24 months, or that your project qualifies as an 'advanced pipeline' project
Line up written endorsements from your employer, the ACIAR project leaders and your primary supervisor - all three are required
Sit IELTS, TOEFL or PTE no more than 6 months before applying, or be ready to test on receipt of the outcome
Write the research proposal so gender equity, social inclusion and climate change are addressed in both the approach and the intended outcomes, and tie it to a development priority of your country
Read the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook before applying, since JAF applicants are bound by Australia Awards conditions including the scholarship contract with the Commonwealth
common_rejection_risks: No current or recent ACIAR project link - the Fellowship is not open to general applicants
Missing endorsement from the employer, the ACIAR project leaders or the primary supervisor; the factsheet warns that missing mandatory documents may affect eligibility
Australian citizenship, permanent residency, or applying for a visa to live in Australia permanently
A coursework Master's application, which is not eligible - only Masters by Research or PhD
A research proposal that does not address gender equity, social inclusion and climate change or a country development priority
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Beyond the published entitlements (full tuition, return airfare, a living-expenses contribution, an establishment allowance and the Introductory Academic Program), costs such as family accompaniment, dependants' costs and gaps during pre-course English may remain with the scholar; the exact allowance values are set by the department and should be confirmed in the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook.
document_audit: Endorsements must come from three parties - employer, ACIAR project leaders and primary supervisor - so start collecting them months before the round opens
The English test recency rule (within the last 6 months at the time of applying) can silently expire an otherwise valid certificate
Applications run through OASIS under the 'ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships' award program - selecting the wrong Australia Awards program sends the file to the wrong assessment
The proposal must satisfy both ACIAR's research framing rules and the Australian institution's admission requirements
alerts: Applications for the 2027 intake are closed; the recent pattern is a 1 February to 30 April window, so prepare for an early-year opening

Award holders are bound by Australia Awards conditions, including the requirement to leave Australia for a minimum of two years after completing the scholarship - failure to do so incurs a debt for the total accrued cost of the scholarship (confirm in the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook)
An offer is only valid for the Australian academic year following the calendar year in which the offer is made
Women now make up at least half of new Fellows, and climate-focused research currently has dedicated allocated places
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in OASIS, select the ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships award program, submit the completed application with endorsements and proposal during the annual window, then sign the Commonwealth contract if selected.
